title: Interleaved Context Reconstruction and Loss-Tolerant Tracing Hooks
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Improve Redwood's request instrumentation by implementing runtime hooks and SDK middleware that can reconstruct trace context when carriers are interleaved or partially lost across async boundaries. The goal is to reduce dropped spans and incorrect parent-child relationships in high-concurrency, async-heavy workloads (Node/Python/Go) while keeping overhead sub-microsecond for hot paths.
goals: Provide a loss-tolerant tracing hook layer that can recover context from partial carriers or timing heuristics
Expose a lightweight middleware shim for language SDKs to surface reconstructed context to user spans
Allow dynamic sampling adjustments when reconstruction confidence is low to preserve observability signal
Ship canary across Redwood-hosted runtime and SDKs with metrics/dashboards to monitor improvement
scope: Runtime-level instrumentation and SDK middleware changes. Support for Node.js (async_hooks), Python (contextvars/asyncio), and Go (context.Context) will be implemented in parallel. Does NOT include UI changes beyond adding observability dashboards and rollout flags in Console. Backwards-compatible: when reconstruction fails, fall back to existing propagation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end test demonstrating correct span parentage in a synthesized interleaving workload with 95%+ reconstruction accuracy
CPU overhead measured on p50/p95 under benchmark workload < 2% compared to baseline for average request sizes
Canary rollout with traffic shaping shows stable error rates and no negative impact on tail latency
Relevant Console dashboard widgets showing reconstructed-span counts, reconstruction confidence histogram, and sampling adjustments
design_decisions: Use a probabilistic reconstruction algorithm that combines timestamp proximity, span-name fingerprints, and id-prefix heuristics instead of deterministic backfills
Keep reconstructed spans marked with a tag (reconstructed=true) so downstream analysis can filter or treat them differently
Implement dual-path instrumentation: fast-path that does no reconstruction for low-latency critical routes and a diagnostic-path enabled by rollout flags
Expose an opt-in config for customers to increase reconstruction aggressiveness (higher recall at cost of potential false parents)
technical_notes: Node prototype uses async_hooks to attach a lightweight context token; when token missing, use an in-memory sliding window to match incoming carriers by id prefix and timestamp delta
Python implementation leverages contextvars with a fallback coroutine-local ring buffer for short-lived context resurrection
Go implementation augments context.Context with a compact carrier fingerprint; runtime shim records recent carrier fingerprints per goroutine pool
Sampling controller will take reconstruction confidence score (0-100) and map to sample-decisions via weighted thresholds to avoid over-sampling noisy reconstructions
All reconstructed events must include deterministic metadata: reconstruction_version, confidence_score, heuristic_sources
tasks: Prototype reconstruction algorithm (Node) and validate on internal interleaving harness
Implement middleware shim for Node SDK and add unit/integration tests
Implement matching mechanisms for Python and Go SDKs
Add reconstruction metadata to span model and ensure ingestion pipeline accepts new fields
Create Console panels for reconstructed span metrics and rollout controls
Prepare canary rollout plan and rollback criteria
Update docs/SDK CHANGELOG and instrumented examples
